subject: ShelfWave morning surge - streaming hiccup and interim steps
messages:
From: Jason Li <jason.li@openretail.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-09-04 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Realtime stream stalls this morning (US-east)

Hi Neha,

We started seeing elevated latency and repeated short stalls on streaming chat at ~09:05 UTC this morning. The client receives chunks for ~8-12 tokens, then the stream pauses for 1-3s before resuming. This impacts our live agent handoff and causes message duplication.

Key details:
- App: ShelfWave mobile (iOS/Android) using Redwood JS SDK 1.6.2
- Model: redwood-3b-gen-quant, stream=true, max_tokens=512
- Affected region: us-east (primary), intermittent on us-west but less severe
- First observed: 2028-09-04T09:05:20Z

Attached are client logs and a short screen capture. Can you confirm if this is a platform-side regression or anything on our side? We have a major morning ramp and this is customer-visible.

Thanks,
Jason
Product Ops | OpenRetail

Attachments: client-logs-20280904.txt (snippet)

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Jason Li <jason.li@openretail.com>, Shelly Ramos <shelly@openretail.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-09-04 09:28:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Realtime stream stalls this morning (US-east)

Jason — thanks for the clear reproduction notes and logs. We're looking into this now. Quick interim steps you can apply immediately to reduce customer impact:

1) Switch to non-streaming responses for critical paths (response_mode: "complete") — this avoids chunked backpressure and should reduce perceived stalls while we triage.
2) Increase client read timeout to 15s (temporary) and implement exponential backoff on stream reconnects (start 300ms, max 2s).
3) Reduce max_tokens to 256 for high-traffic flows; smaller responses reduce tokenization and buffer pressure.
4) Enable SDK fallback: set streaming_fallback: true so the client will request the same answer without streaming if the stream stalls.

We're starting an immediate investigation on our side. Can we enable a temporary routing override to a compatible runtime variant for your traffic (dedicated-us-east-compat) while we roll mitigations? Please reply with authorization and any blackout windows.

I'll loop in engineering with traces and we'll share an ETA within 30–45 minutes.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0198

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, Jason Li <jason.li@openretail.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-09-04 09:55:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Realtime stream stalls this morning (US-east) — engineering update

Quick update from infra: we see a correlated rise in small-buffer backpressure across a subset of us-east shards coincident with the ShelfWave ramp. Root cause appears to be a tokenization windowing regression in the streaming path that increases flush latency under bursty traffic.

Actions taken (in progress):
- Applied a temporary traffic steering rule: ShelfWave production routes to dedicated-us-east-compat (non-stream-optimized runtime) — this is live as of 09:50 UTC.
- Rolling a hotfix to the streaming buffer flusher (v1.9.3-hotpatch) that eliminates the extra flush wait; deploy target ETA ~ 11:30 UTC.
- Collected per-shard traces and pulled diag bundles (attached). We'll follow up with the incident timeline and postmortem notes.

Short-term client guidance (confirming Neha's notes):
- If you can't switch away from streaming immediately, enable streaming_fallback and set a client-side reconnect with jitter — we expect the steering rule to materially reduce stalls within minutes.

I'll post a brief incident timeline and notify once the hotfix is live.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior SRE | Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident-timeline-20280904.pdf, diag-logs-20280904.tar.gz

From: Jason Li <jason.li@openretail.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-09-04 11:03:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Realtime stream stalls this morning (US-east)

Thanks Neha / Marcus — we authorized the temporary routing override. After the steering rule went live we saw the stall rate drop from ~18% of sessions to <2% within 6 minutes. Enabling streaming_fallback on the client also helped for a handful of edge devices.

Shelly and I are available for a 30m postmortem next week — suggest Tue 2028-09-11 15:00 UTC. Please send a calendar invite and any pre-read (incident timeline + mitigation notes).

Appreciate the quick response.

— Jason
Jason Li
Product Ops | OpenRetail
